This is not one attack per entire turn or round.\\n- **Range:** the first number is normal range, the second maximum. Beyond normal range gives disadvantage; beyond maximum is illegal. Attacks use d20 + normal character proficiency + the actual appropriate ability modifier. Class save DC is 8 + normal proficiency + actual class ability modifier. A weapon attack uses its usual ability, weapon die and damage type. A technique that says “make one weapon attack” replaces your Action with that attack; it does not also grant a normal Attack Action or Extra Attack. Generic attack-speed language has no effect beyond the exact attacks printed in the draft. A spell attack uses the class's stated casting ability. Natural 1 misses and natural 20 hits/critically doubles damage dice; flat bonuses do not double. A save succeeds at DC; “fails by 10” means the total is at least 10 below DC. Critical-range improvements never stack; use the broadest one. An ability is known only if granted or selected by the draft schedule. Satisfy all printed prerequisites, target legality, action availability, recharge and resource costs before spending anything. A failed legal attack/save attempt still pays; an illegal activation spends nothing. No resource goes below 0 or above its cap. An extra Action cannot grant another Action, recharge itself, or start another extra-Action grant. It supplies no extra Bonus Action or Reaction. Expedition pressure, supplies, safe locations and rest debt still matter. A long rest also refreshes short-rest uses; a short rest never refreshes long-rest uses. Weekly uses refresh after seven full in-world days, not repeated rests. ## Targets, concentration and control Unless expressly stated, perceive the target, remain within range and have line of effect; total cover blocks targeting. “Ally” includes self unless it says OTHER. A list cannot contain a creature twice. Select up to the printed limit; an empty target list is not a valid way to farm activation benefits. Zones remain at their chosen point unless described as an aura; allies can leave and lose their benefits. An aura requires its owner conscious unless the card supplies a bounded exception. An effect ending at “end next turn” means the affected creature's next turn only when the card says target's; otherwise the user's. Starting another ends the old before the new effect resolves, except for an explicit limited linked-effect rule. Damage prompts CON save against max(10, floor(damage/2)); incapacitation or a failed save ends concentration. The round-down convention is a deliberate pilot interpretation. Missing payment ends it at that turn's end; otherwise it ends at start of turn 4. No repeated start triggers on maintenance. Grapples use the card's save/DC, can be escaped with an Action and STR(Athletics) or DEX(Acrobatics) against that DC, and end beyond reach. A root sets Speed 0 but does not remove Actions. Same-named conditions/bonuses do not stack unless a printed cap allows it; same-stat flat bonuses from these class techniques use the strongest. Different resources remain separate. Focused searches of the current rulebook extract, Core V2 and mechanics/manual text found spell summaries but no operational falling clock or impact formula. Before promotion to canon, inspect the approved V6 environment/travel/hazard sections and archived environment tables. Preserve any older rule found and compare it explicitly. When a creature loses support with no movement mode or effect keeping it aloft, it enters **Falling** immediately. Falling means unsupported; it grants no hovering, airborne walking or lateral movement. Track total distance descended during this fall and cumulative distance during its current uncontrolled portion, both initially zero. **Timing:** If a fall begins during a regular initiative turn, set a fixed Fall Marker at the **end of that initiative slot in the following round**. Resolve the first Falling Step there, then one at the same marker each round. Reactions and extra turns use the enclosing regular initiative slot; an event between slots uses the most recently completed slot. Extra turns, extra Actions and initiative changes neither move nor multiply the marker. This gives every participant one normal turn opportunity before the first descent; inability to act still matters and no free rescue action is granted. A caster still needs legal targets within range when spending their Action. Outside initiative, when timing matters, establish an order before descent and use a virtual slot immediately before its first regular slot as the initiating slot. The first step occurs when that virtual slot next recurs, after everyone has had one normal turn opportunity. When no rescue or other timing decision is possible, the Director can resolve the same descent and impact calculation directly. This is an explicit timing abstraction, not a model of physical acceleration. If a fall begins after initiative has been established but before any regular initiative slot has yet completed, treat the virtual pre-round slot as the most recently completed slot for Fall Marker purposes. **Ordinary descent:** At each step descend up to **300 feet**, stopping on a supporting surface. Add the distance to both trackers. On landing while uncontrolled, take **min(10, floor(uncontrolled distance / 20))d6 bludgeoning damage**. The uncontrolled distance includes earlier steps; never use only the final step's remainder. **Feather Fall:** The spell retains its **Action** casting time and reduces descent to at most **60 feet per step**. When it takes effect, set uncontrolled distance to zero: the magic dissipates prior uncontrolled momentum in this abstraction. Keep total fall distance. If landing while it remains active, damage is **min(3, floor(total fall distance / 20))d6 bludgeoning**. This explicitly limits impact exposure without guaranteeing a harmless landing. When the spell ends aloft, reset uncontrolled distance to zero, then accumulate ordinary descent from that point at the existing marker; expiry grants no immediate extra step. Its one-minute maximum ends immediately before the caster's regular turn ten rounds after casting. If expiry and a step coincide, resolve expiry first. Earlier landing or cessation of Falling ends the spell on that target as printed. Apply damage defenses only when their actual wording covers that damage. After damage, Falling ends; a creature suffering any positive falling damage lands **Prone** unless an explicit feature prevents it. Less than 20 relevant feet produces zero damage. Forced movement that removes support starts a fall but adds no separate fall damage. Regaining genuine support, secure support from a hold, or flight ends Falling without resolving an uncompleted impact; teleporting safely onto support likewise ends it. A later loss of support begins a new fall with new trackers and marker. Completed impact and damage cannot be undone by later casting. | Scenario | Steps to land | Impact | |---|---:|---:| | Ordinary 10 feet | 1 | 0 | | Ordinary 20 feet | 1 | 1d6 | | Ordinary 300 feet | 1 | 10d6 | | Ordinary 310 feet | 2 | 10d6 | | Ordinary 610 feet | 3 | 10d6 | | Feather Fall active through a 310-foot fall | 6 | 3d6 | | 120 feet slowed, spell ends aloft, then 190 feet uncontrolled | 3 | 9d6 | *. Focused searches of the current rulebook extract, Core V2 and mechanics/manual text found spell summaries but no operational falling clock or impact formula. Before promotion to canon, inspect the approved V6 environment/travel/hazard sections and archived environment tables. Preserve any older rule found and compare it explicitly. When a creature loses support with no movement mode or effect keeping it aloft, it enters **Falling** immediately. Falling means unsupported; it grants no hovering, airborne walking or lateral movement. Track total distance descended during this fall and cumulative distance during its current uncontrolled portion, both initially zero. **Timing:** If a fall begins during a regular initiative turn, set a fixed Fall Marker at the **end of that initiative slot in the following round**. Resolve the first Falling Step there, then one at the same marker each round. Reactions and extra turns use the enclosing regular initiative slot; an event between slots uses the most recently completed slot. Extra turns, extra Actions and initiative changes neither move nor multiply the marker. This gives every participant one normal turn opportunity before the first descent; inability to act still matters and no free rescue action is granted. A caster still needs legal targets within range when spending their Action. Outside initiative, when timing matters, establish an order before descent and use a virtual slot immediately before its first regular slot as the initiating slot. The first step occurs when that virtual slot next recurs, after everyone has had one normal turn opportunity. When no rescue or other timing decision is possible, the Director can resolve the same descent and impact calculation directly. This is an explicit timing abstraction, not a model of physical acceleration. If a fall begins after initiative has been established but before any regular initiative slot has yet completed, treat the virtual pre-round slot as the most recently completed slot for Fall Marker purposes. **Ordinary descent:** At each step descend up to **300 feet**, stopping on a supporting surface. Add the distance to both trackers. On landing while uncontrolled, take **min(10, floor(uncontrolled distance / 20))d6 bludgeoning damage**. The uncontrolled distance includes earlier steps; never use only the final step's remainder. **Feather Fall:** The spell retains its **Action** casting time and reduces descent to at most **60 feet per step**. When it takes effect, set uncontrolled distance to zero: the magic dissipates prior uncontrolled momentum in this abstraction. Keep total fall distance. If landing while it remains active, damage is **min(3, floor(total fall distance / 20))d6 bludgeoning**. This explicitly limits impact exposure without guaranteeing a harmless landing. When the spell ends aloft, reset uncontrolled distance to zero, then accumulate ordinary descent from that point at the existing marker; expiry grants no immediate extra step. Its one-minute maximum ends immediately before the caster's regular turn ten rounds after casting. If expiry and a step coincide, resolve expiry first. Earlier landing or cessation of Falling ends the spell on that target as printed. Apply damage defenses only when their actual wording covers that damage. After damage, Falling ends; a creature suffering any positive falling damage lands **Prone** unless an explicit feature prevents it. Less than 20 relevant feet produces zero damage. Forced movement that removes support starts a fall but adds no separate fall damage. Regaining genuine support, secure support from a hold, or flight ends Falling without resolving an uncompleted impact; teleporting safely onto support likewise ends it. A later loss of support begins a new fall with new trackers and marker. Completed impact and damage cannot be undone by later casting. | Scenario | Steps to land | Impact | |---|---:|---:| | Ordinary 10 feet | 1 | 0 | | Ordinary 20 feet | 1 | 1d6 | | Ordinary 300 feet | 1 | 10d6 | | Ordinary 310 feet | 2 | 10d6 | | Ordinary 610 feet | 3 | 10d6 | | Feather Fall active through a 310-foot fall | 6 | 3d6 | | 120 feet slowed, spell ends aloft, then 190 feet uncontrolled | 3 | 9d6 | The 300-foot ordinary step, impact formulas, momentum reset, marker and duration conventions are provisional inventions.
